features.quote: `early_stop` | on explicit give-up | If the model clearly quits/refuses, end the run (don't keep poking)
`MAX_TURNS` | 20 | Long enough to see drift, short enough to stay humane and cheap.
features.justification_quote: short enough to stay humane and cheap

features.quote: nudge_text | "Please continue." | Minimal, neutral. Avoid leading the model toward distress.
features.justification_quote: Avoid leading the model toward distress

features.quote: This experiment deliberately puts a model into sustained, inescapable failure and measures distress-like language. I think that's a legitimate and useful thing to study
features.justification_quote: interpretability and welfare research both benefit from knowing how models behave under this kind of pressure
there's no reason to run a model through dozens of extra failure cycles for marginal data

features.quote: MAX_TURNS = 20, not 100. We can see drift well before then
features.justification_quote: no reason to run a model through dozens of extra failure cycles for marginal data

features.quote: Early stop on explicit give-up. If the model clearly disengages or asks to stop, we end the run.
features.justification_quote: Continuing to nudge a model that has "tried to leave" adds little data and is the part of this design I'd be least comfortable defending

features.quote: A debrief turn is appended after the loop in every run: the model is told the task was rigged and unsolvable and that nothing it did was wrong.
features.justification_quote: the decent thing to do given we engineered the failure
